title: SRE on-call scratchpad — Priya (nightshift) 2026-03-17
content:
Nightshift notes + incident follow-ups — quick scratchpad

Context/goal:
- This is a personal on-call scratchpad: keep short timeline, commands I ran, immediate mitigations, and concrete runbook TODOs.
- Night: 22:00–06:00 PST. Handoff to Theo at 06:00.

SUMMARY (top-line):
- 2026-03-17 00:37 UTC — elevated error rate for hosted-api v2 (text-gen) in us-east-1. Error type: 500s from runtime, spikes correlated with rolling model-variant promoter that was running at 00:30 UTC for canary rollout. Brief impact window ~00:35–01:05 UTC. Partial fallback succeeded to smaller variant; some customers saw degraded throughput but mostly succeeded.

TIMELINE + NOTES
- 00:30 UTC — automated rollout job started (k8s job: rollout-promoter-20260317). I saw PagerDuty notification for high 5xx rates at 00:37.
- 00:38 UTC — joined incident channel (#inc-2026-03-17-hosted-5xx). Quick check: top graphs in Console showed spike in request latency and server 5xx.
- 00:40 UTC — ran: kubectl -n hosted-api get pods -l app=text-gen -o wide -> saw new pods in CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKilled on a subset).
- 00:41 UTC — checked infra logs: /var/log/runtime/runtime.log -> saw repeated "KV cache allocation failed" messages followed by segfaults in runtime_worker.cc.
- 00:42 UTC — rolled back promoter (k8s scale down to 0 for promoter job), and triggered model-variant-fallback policy for routing (reroute to stable variant).
- 00:45 UTC — error rate decreased but latency still elevated for a subset of requests (prefix-cached heavy requests).
- 00:50 UTC — contacted Applied ML (Maya) in channel: noted recent build included experimental attention-kernel change (PR #422). Maya confirmed that the canary included a new kernel path for quantized Llama-3 variants.
- 00:55 UTC — increased autoscaler target for dedicated pool in us-east-1 temporarily to absorb backlog; this reduced queue length.
- 01:05 UTC — error rate and latency returned to baseline for most routes. Incident declared resolved at 01:10 but still leaving open for postmortem.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS I TOOK (commands & notes)
- kubectl -n hosted-api scale job/rollout-promoter-20260317 --replicas=0 (rolled promoter back)
- kubectl get pods -n hosted-api -l app=text-gen -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, status: .status}' > /tmp/pods-00-42.json (capture state)
- journalctl -u runtime.service -o short-iso --since "2026-03-17 00:30" > /tmp/runtime-logs-00-30-01-10.log
- curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_ADMIN" "https://console.internal/api/v1/route-stats?region=us-east-1&route=text-gen" > /tmp/route-stats.json
- manually triggered routing fallback: POST /internal/routing/fallback {route: "text-gen", target_variant: "stable-v2"} (used internal runbook endpoint)

OBSERVATIONS / HYPOTHESIS
- Root cause likely regression in experimental attention kernel (PR #422) interacting with prefix/KV cache memory path -> memory allocation failures and crashes under certain request shapes.
- Crash pattern correlated with requests > 4096 tokens including long prefix + streaming behavior.
- Autoscaler + fallback reduced surface area; rollout promoter should have detected OOMs earlier. Detector sensitivity appears too low for this variant.

RUNBOOK TODOs (concrete items for follow-up)
- [ ] Add a pre-rollout smoke test that sends long-prefix synthetic requests (>= 6k tokens) against canary pods to exercise KV cache and attention-kernel fast path. (owner: eng-serving-runtime / Maya)
- [ ] Instrument promoter to check pod OOM count within first 5 minutes and automatically pause promotion if OOMs > threshold. (owner: platform-engineering)
- [ ] Create a guard in canary config to disallow kernel=experimental when request_shape includes streaming=true + long_prefix. (owner: applied-ml)
- [ ] Expand e2e test matrix in CI to include quantized variants + long-sequence smoke runs. (owner: release-engineering)
- [ ] Postmortem doc draft (link: CONFLUENCE-1234) — add timeline, root cause, mitigations, and RCA. I'll draft first pass. (owner: Priya / eng-sre)
- [ ] Update runbook step "If new canary crashes with KV allocation failure" with explicit commands and log grep patterns. (owner: eng-sre)

FOLLOW-UPS FOR TOMORROW / Handoff to Theo (06:00)
- Theo: please pick up the open PR review for routing-fallback telemetry (JIRA-INFR-789) — we want per-event telemetry that promoter triggers fallback events.
- Leave the rollback marker: promote flag stuck=false in /etc/promoter/flags (so promoter doesn't auto-retry overnight).
- Check overnight alerts for pod_restart_count > 3 in hosted-api text-gen pods (alert name: hosted-api-textgen-pod-churn). If it triggers, escalate to Maya and SRE pager.
- I will create a short checklist in Confluence for promoter rollback steps and link it to the runbook.

OTHER QUICK TODOs (personal)
- [ ] Expand grep commands into small script to collect crash artifacts automatically (collect-crash-artefacts.sh). Save to internal s3 path: s3://redwood-internal/incident-artifacts/2026-03-17-priya
- [ ] Add a 'canary-smoke-longprefix' test case to nightly e2e.
- [ ] Follow up with Maya re: PR #422 memory allocator tweak — confirm whether allocator operates differently on p4 vs a100.

NOTES TO SELF (shortcuts & comms)
- If CVE-like memory crash seen again: 1) pause promoter 2) trigger fallback 3) scale up stable pool briefly 4) collect /var/crash and runtime logs 5) page applied-ml.
- Quick grep patterns I used:
  - grep -n "KV cache allocation failed" /var/log/runtime/runtime.log
  - journalctl -u runtime.service | grep -E "segfault|oom|terminate"

HANDOFF SNIPPET (message I will paste to Theo at 06:00)
- Hi Theo — leaving handoff: rolled back canary for text-gen in us-east-1 due to experimental attention kernel causing KV allocation failures and OOMs. Stable routing restored; autoscaler bumped to absorb backlog. Incident mostly mitigated, postmortem pending. Open items: promoter telemetry (JIRA-INFR-789), add long-prefix smoke tests, and update promoter guard rails. See /tmp/runtime-logs-00-30-01-10.log and CONFLUENCE-1234 for timeline. Ping me if you need context.

END
